fields.name: rule_set_name
fields.label: Rule Set Name
fields.sourceQuote: Rule Set Name: The name of the rule set.
fields.notes: List-page column on the Purchase Order Matching Rules page; row is the selection target for Edit/Copy. Selecting a row under this column is the first step of every edit/copy/unlock procedure (edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md: 'select the rule set row under Rule Set Name').

fields.name: in_use
fields.label: In Use
fields.sourceQuote: In Use: Shows if the matching rule set has been applied against any active invoice (Yes) or has not yet applied (No) in the system.
fields.notes: Both values are explicitly enumerated in the same clause, not a completed guess. GATE: a rule set with In Use = Yes cannot be modified in any way; the admin must Copy it first, or unlock it by breaking the rule set's association to every invoice. THE UNLOCK CONTROL IS OFF THIS PAGE and is therefore NOT emitted as a field of this page (see dropped/change_to_non_po_action): it is the Actions-menu item on the My Invoices end-user page - 'In the Actions menu, click Change to Non-PO.' (tools-guides/change-a-po-based-invoice-policy-to-a-non-po-based-invoice-policy-12786d77.md), full sequence My Invoices > select one or more PO-based invoices > Actions > Change to Non-PO > Select a Policy window > choose a non-PO policy > OK, possibly plus reassignment via Assign. Treat it as an outbound prerequisite dependency of this column. LABEL CONTRADICTION 2:1, NOT RECONCILED: 'Change to Non-PO' (test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md and tools-guides 12786d77.md) vs 'Change to Non PO Invoice option in the Actions menu' (purchase-order-matching-rules-new-experience-6c8fb80f.md). Copy-then-repoint-the-policy is the other documented workaround.

fields.name: associated_policies
fields.label: Associated Policies
fields.sourceQuote: Associated Policies: Shows what Invoice PO policy has been configured to include this PO matching rule set. You select a rule set using the PO Matching Ruleset option in Policies.
fields.notes: Read-only display column showing which Policies (Group 1, already-built page) reference this rule set via the PO Matching Ruleset field there. Outbound dependency only - never re-home PO Matching Ruleset to this page.

fields.name: copy_button
fields.label: Copy
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules, select an existing rule set under Rule Set Name, and then click Copy.
fields.notes: Only documented way to start a new rule set - there is NO 'New' button attested anywhere in the corpus for this page. Also the prescribed workaround for editing a locked (In Use=Yes) rule set (access-purchase-order-matching-rules-8407c500.md: 'use the Copy button to create a copy, edit the rule set as needed'). Full documented sequence (step-1): select under Rule Set Name > Copy > click the 'Copy of...' entry > Rename > type name > press Enter > Done; copy-purchase-order-matching-rules-c6d4106a.md states the copy procedure is identical to Step 1 and adds nothing further (thin, and that is the correct answer). Second-level corroboration that Copy also operates on a selected rule CONDITION, not only a rule set: 'Select an existing rule condition (for example, "Services Under $5000"), and then select Edit, Copy, Delete, or Rename to perform those functions' (match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md, which also carries the scoping caveat 'These instructions cover the new receipt related functions only.'). MERGE NOTE: the fuller sourceQuote from the dropped cross-lens twin ruleSetCopy was adopted here because it names the containing page; both quotes were grep-verified verbatim.

fields.name: rename_button
fields.label: Rename
fields.sourceQuote: click Rename and type a descriptive name for the matching rule set, pressing Enter when you are done.
fields.notes: Renames the auto-generated 'Copy of...' entry produced by Copy. Step 2 of the only documented creation sequence (Copy > Rename > Done). The commit is a KEYSTROKE, not a button - 'pressing Enter when you are done' - which a driver must perform explicitly. Also listed among the actions available on a selected rule condition in match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md.

fields.name: done_button
fields.label: Done
fields.sourceQuote: 3.  Click Done.
fields.notes: Terminal step of the Copy -> Rename -> Done rule-set-creation wizard (Step 1). Distinct from the final rule-set Save at the end of Steps 2/3.

fields.name: edit_button
fields.label: Edit
fields.sourceQuote: On the Purchase Order Matching Rules page, select the rule set, and then click Edit.
fields.notes: Opens the rule set for editing (loosely called 'Purchase Order Matching Set' in edit-purchase-order-matching-rules-604d1e31.md: 'Click Edit to open Purchase Order Matching Set.'). Only available when In Use = No; also becomes available again after the Change to Non-PO unlock action (test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md: 'the rule set has a status of No and can be edited using the Edit button'). NOT to be confused with the 'Edit' link inside the Exception Message dialog (see exception_message) which edits a saved message, not the rule set. ALTERNATE OPEN PATH not to be missed by a driver: configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md documents 'Double-click the rule you want to use, and then, in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules.' - i.e. a double-click on the rule-set row substitutes for the Edit button. Try both.

fields.name: edit_rules_button
fields.label: Edit Rules
fields.sourceQuote: in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears.
fields.notes: Opens the 'Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window' which contains the Rules and Life to Date tabs. CONTRADICTION - TAB DEPTH: step-3-create-the-po-to-request-fields-matching-rules-64eb1c47.md never mentions Edit Rules and instead places the Rules tab one level up ('In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.'). See contradiction 'tab-depth-rules-life-to-date' below; majority tree (2 of 3 topics) is page > Edit > select rule group > Edit Rules > [Rules | Life to Date]. Also used in Step 4 for condition-based sub-rules ('select the new condition, and then click Edit Rules to specify what should happen').

fields.name: rules_tab
fields.label: Rules
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Set, click the Rules tab.
fields.notes: Corpus type unattested as tab vs. window heading - recorded as 'unknown' rather than guessing. Holds the field-to-field (one-to-one) matching rules, the Tolerance controls, Exception Message, and Allow Submit/Approve. Part of contradiction 'tab-depth-rules-life-to-date'.

fields.name: life_to_date_tab
fields.label: Life to Date
fields.sourceQuote: Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:
fields.notes: Holds the 6-row Life to Date rule-type checkbox table (see life_to_date_rule_selection) and the Overage Tolerance controls. Part of contradiction 'tab-depth-rules-life-to-date'.

fields.name: currency_field
fields.label: Currency
fields.sourceQuote: Currency: Choose the base currency your company uses. Conversions for alternate currencies used on incoming invoices will be calculated automatically and applied by the system.
fields.notes: Listed as a 4th tolerance option in step-3's reading of the Tolerance contradiction ('Currency: Choose the base currency...'). Underlying exchange-rate activation is NOT a control on this page - it is on by default and configured via the Expense Admin module (see dependencyCandidate 'exchange-rates-off-page'). No enumerated currency list found in the corpus. MERGED FROM THE DROPPED CROSS-LENS TWIN (toleranceCurrency): on the Life to Date tab step-2 pairs Currency with Value ('Value AND Currency, - OR - Percentage'), whereas step-3 lists Currency as a FOURTH tolerance option - that is one contested half of the recorded tolerance contradiction, which is why this record carries the neutral name 'currency_field' rather than 'toleranceCurrency'; naming it after one reading would silently reconcile a live contradiction. No currency roster is published anywhere in the corpus, so validValues stays empty.

fields.name: change_button
fields.label: Change
fields.sourceQuote: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.
fields.notes: Opens the Exception Message editor/list from the Rules or Life to Date tab. First step of the fifth dialog sequence. Attested twice in configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md (steps 5 and 10, i.e. from the Rules tab AND the Life to Date tab) and again in step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md. SUB-DIALOG SCOPE: this is not a control on the rule-set list page - it sits in the rule-group rules window and opens a nested editor.

fields.name: new_button
fields.label: New
fields.sourceQuote: add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.
fields.notes: Creates a new exception message inside the Exception Message editor opened via Change. SCOPE, so this never drifts up the tree: there is NO New button for creating a rule SET on this page - creation is Copy > Rename > Done. GAP RECORDED, NOT FABRICATED: the editor's third control, Edit ('edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit'), is attested in the same sentence but was emitted by no lens and is therefore absent from this roster; a driver told to modify an existing exception message has no record to drive.

fields.name: save_button
fields.label: Save
fields.sourceQuote: 9.  Click Save.
fields.notes: Generic Save control that recurs across this page's procedures: final Save of the rule set (Step 3 ends '9. Click Save.'; Step 2 similarly ends its own tolerance/exception-message configuration and proceeds to Step 3), Save inside the Exception Message editor ('then click Save'), and Save at the end of the condition-based rule group workflow (step-4: 'Click Insert to add any addition conditions, and then click Save when you are done.' and 'Add any additional rules, clicking Update after each new rule to add it to the row, then click Save.'). Consolidated as one control since the corpus never distinguishes it by a different label; context is noted here rather than duplicating the field.

fields.name: add_button
fields.label: Add
fields.sourceQuote: Click Add to insert this rule into the rows under Rules.
fields.notes: Same-labeled Add button recurs in multiple contexts on this page: inserts a completed field-to-field rule into the Rules list (Step 3, and configure-three-way step 7: '7. Click Add.'); adds a condition-based rule group under a named rules group (step-4: 'Select the named rule group within which the condition-based rule set will be included, then click Add.'); and, in the confirmation-type sub-configuration, adds a new rule condition (match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md: 'Add a new rule condition by selecting the Rule Set (for example "Default"), and then selecting Add').

fields.name: insert_button
fields.label: Insert
fields.sourceQuote: Click Insert to add any addition conditions, and then click Save when you are done.
fields.notes: Adds another condition row inside the Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions dialog. SAP typo preserved: 'any addition conditions' for 'any additional conditions'.

fields.name: update_button
fields.label: Update
fields.sourceQuote: Click Update to add the rule to the row.
fields.notes: Commits a condition-based rule (created via Edit Rules) into its row within the named rules group; repeat then final Save.

fields.name: delete_button
fields.label: Delete
fields.sourceQuote: delete the rule by selecting and clicking Delete.
fields.notes: Deletes a default or added rule row from the Rules tab. Also documented as an action for a rule condition in the confirmation-type sub-configuration: 'select Edit, Copy, Delete, or Rename to perform those functions' (match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md).

fields.name: edit_confirmation_button
fields.label: Edit Confirmation
fields.sourceQuote: Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window, choosing a confirmation type based on the rule group.
fields.notes: Opens the Select Confirmation Type window (see confirmation_type). Corroborated in match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md, applied to either the Rule Set itself or a rule condition: 'select an existing Rule Set ("Default") or rule condition ("Services Under $5000"), and then select Edit Confirmation to create or change the confirmation type.' MERGED FROM THE DROPPED CROSS-LENS TWIN (editConfirmation): note match-rules-and-rule-sets-87e69410.md's scoping caveat 'These instructions cover the new receipt related functions only.'; the confirmation type can be driven by Spend Category, Capital Expense Status and Amount Threshold; and the instructional TEXT for each type is NOT edited here - it is edited in the Localization tool, a page not yet in this graph, so that dependency legitimately stays unresolved.

fields.name: rule_groups_list
fields.label: Rule Groups
fields.sourceQuote: in the Rule Groups list, select a rule group and click Edit Rules. The Purchase Order Matching Rule Group rules window appears.
fields.notes: The selectable list of named rules groups inside an opened rule set. No enumerated membership beyond 'Default' and any condition-based groups the admin has added. DEFAULT IS A VALUE HERE, NOT A CONTROL (candidate default_rule_group_select was dropped for that reason and its evidence folded in): 'Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).' (step-2-create-the-life-to-date-matching-rule-set-dc296ae6.md) - Default is the shipped, pre-seeded named rules group and every worked procedure starts from it. AMBIGUITY LEFT OPEN DELIBERATELY: 'Default' names TWO different objects in this corpus - the shipped named rules GROUP (the step-2 quote above) and the shipped rule SET ('A Default rule set is provided', create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md - a TRUNCATED file; 'Copy the Default rule set', test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md). The corpus does not disambiguate them and this record does not either. Membership beyond Default is tenant-built and is never enumerated, so validValues stays empty.

fields.name: life_to_date_rule_selection
fields.label: Selection
fields.sourceQuote: Click the Life to Date tab, then select the check box next to the rule type to activate using the table below:
fields.notes: THE PRIMARY SETTINGS TABLE OF THIS PAGE. A 6-row two-column markdown table (Selection | Description) on the Life to Date tab; all six rows enumerated here and again, with their descriptions, in valueSetCandidates. INDENTED-TABLE TRAP: this table is nested inside a numbered step, so grep -c '^| ' returns 0 while grep -cP '^\s*\|' returns 22 - a census anchored on '^|' would have missed it entirely. 'Selection' is the literal column header the corpus gives; the corpus never states a separate on-screen label for the control, and the control is a set of check boxes ('select the check box next to the rule type'), so more than one value may be active at once ('Repeat by selecting a check box for each option you want to include.'). Label drift on the fifth row: the table and configure-three-way-matching L60 write 'Match against Received Quantity' while configure-three-way-matching L27 writes 'Matched against Received Quantity' - recorded as a contradiction, not reconciled.

fields.name: purchase_order_field
fields.label: Purchase Order
fields.sourceQuote: Under Purchase Order, select the PO field to match to the invoice (they will change depending on the field selected in the step above).
fields.notes: On the Rules tab, paired with Payment Request. validValues EMPTY for the same reason: the corpus explicitly says the options change with the Payment Request selection above it and never publishes the catalog. The only enumerated case is the Line Item – Receipt pair ('Line Quantity and Received Quantity' / 'Receipt Associated and Receipt Associated'), held as a valueSetCandidate.

fields.name: overage_tolerance
fields.label: Overage Tolerance
fields.sourceQuote: In the Overage Tolerance section, select Value or Percentage.
fields.notes: ONLY attestation of the label 'Overage Tolerance' in the corpus; it appears on the Life to Date tab after selecting Match against Received Quantity. Exactly two options are enumerated. This is in tension with step-2, which describes the Life to Date tolerance refinement as UNLABELLED and offers a THIRD option (Currency, paired with Value) - recorded as a contradiction. The worked semantics are documented: Value is an absolute threshold ('if the Value is 100 and the Quantity Received on this PO line is 1000, invoice(s) at or above 1100 will trigger the exception'); Percentage is relative. fieldType 'radio' is inferred from 'select Value or Percentage' being mutually exclusive - the corpus never names a widget.

fields.name: exception_message
fields.label: Exception Message
fields.sourceQuote: Exception Message: Click Change and add a message by clicking New, or edit an existing message by selecting it and clicking Edit, then click Save.
fields.notes: Lives in the Exception Message area of the rule-group rules window, on the Rules tab ('The Exception Message option is available on the Rules tab and will only display when the user triggers the configured rule.', refine-the-rules-include-an-exception-message-c174b2b6.md). This is the FIFTH dialog of the page: Change opens a message editor with its own New / Edit / Save controls, and a driver cannot set an exception message without traversing it. Corroborated cross-directory by how-to-deal-with-exceptions-using-matching-rules-options-171867ad.md. The message text itself is free text - the corpus enumerates no values. The identical instruction also appears in step-2, i.e. the editor is reachable from both the Rules and Life to Date tabs.

fields.name: allow_submit_approve
fields.label: Allow Submit/Approve
fields.sourceQuote: Allow Submit/Approve: Select this check box to allow submission and processing of the invoice even if an exception is triggered.
fields.notes: In the Options section of the Rules tab ('This "override" action is selected by using the Allow Submit/Approve feature in the Options section of the Rules tab.', refine-the-rules-allow-submission-despite-tolerance-9b96d467.md); also offered alongside Exception Message on the Life to Date tab per step-2. validValues is EMPTY ON PURPOSE: the corpus documents only the selected state ('Select this check box to allow...'). It never enumerates or names a cleared/unselected value, so no No/Off/Cleared value is invented here - completing the pair is exactly the defect this project has already paid for twice.

fields.name: confirmation_type
fields.label: Confirmation Type
fields.sourceQuote: These outcomes are called confirmation types, and there are four types:
fields.notes: Set in the Select Confirmation Type window, reached from the rule-group roster: 'Do this by clicking Edit Confirmation to open the Select Confirmation Type window, choosing a confirmation type based on the rule group.' (step-5). The four values come from the numbered prose catalog in confirmation-types-b4a94761.md; step-5's 3-row markdown table gives the same three non-None types WITH THE INTERNAL CODES INVC / RIND / RCEN, which appear nowhere else in the corpus, plus their default message text - both catalogs are enumerated in full as separate valueSetCandidates. A fifth documented state exists for rule CONDITIONS only, not for the rule set: 'Parent choice displays for rule conditions only, and indicates the choice made for the parent Rule Set will be used.' - deliberately NOT added to validValues because the corpus scopes it to conditions and never lists it among the types. HARD GATE from another surface: unless Is Receipt Required is Yes on the PO line, none of this is evaluated.

fields.name: named_rules_group_name
fields.label: Name
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules, type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name.
fields.notes: REPAIRED (merge of the cross-lens twins name_field / named_rules_group_name / namedRulesGroupName - one control, one record; name_field is listed in dropped). Free-text name typed in the rule-group rules window after clicking Edit Rules on a selected group. AMBIGUITY RECORDED, NOT SETTLED - this is the repair the refuter demanded: the cited sentence says 'type a descriptive name for the new rule in Name', i.e. the corpus says RULE. The reading that Name names the new NAMED RULES GROUP is INFERRED from the preceding step of the same procedure ('Select Default, then click Edit Rules (this named rules group is the basis for your new rules group).') and from the glossary ('Named Rules Group: Any rule existing within ("under") the Matching Rule Set, for example, a condition-based rule group.', terminology-d3b9f043.md). The corpus does not disambiguate whether this Name names the new rule or the new named rules group; a driver should expect either. The record name retains the 'named_rules_group' wording only as a page-scoped identifier - it is NOT an assertion; the graph already holds six other fields labelled 'Name' (Policies, Image Handling, Audit Rules x2, Expense Types, Company Locations), so a bare 'Name' identifier was rejected. Distinct from Rule Set Name (the read-only list column on the page itself, set via Rename). A naming CONVENTION, not a validation rule, is documented for the rule set: 'the best practice naming convention is something similar to "Test – Rule Set V1"' (test-and-change-match-rule-sets-49f57319.md) - note the EN DASH in that convention string. No length, character or uniqueness constraint exists anywhere in the corpus.

fields.name: value_percentage_radio
fields.label: Value or Percentage
fields.sourceQuote: If applicable, in the Tolerance section, select None, Within, or Custom, and then select Value or Percentage.
fields.notes: REPAIRED (merge of the cross-lens twins value_percentage_radio / toleranceBasis - one control, one record; toleranceBasis is listed in dropped). QUOTE UPGRADED: the fuller line from the same file was adopted because it LOCATES the control 'in the Tolerance section' - which matters, because a near-identical Value/Percentage pair exists in the Overage Tolerance section on the Life to Date tab (see overage_tolerance). Both quotes were grep-verified verbatim; the shorter one was a strict substring. Secondary refinement shown after a Tolerance choice other than None. Value = 'Specify a number at or above that at which the rule set will trigger an exception.' Percentage = 'Choose a percent above which the rule set will trigger a flag.' Both options are enumerated inside the cited clause, so nothing is inferred; fieldType 'radio' is inferred from the mutually exclusive 'select Value or Percentage' - the corpus never names the widget. The LABEL is derived from the two option names: the corpus never gives this control a name of its own. Corroborated generically by amounts-and-tolerances-ab795b1f.md ('this can be refined by including tolerance levels applying to the absolute currency value, or to a percentage', which also states multiple rules may run on the same field), and refine-the-rules-combine-the-life-to-date-and-rules-rule-types-2b46973f.md documents a tolerance value of ZERO as legitimate.

fields.name: level_field
fields.label: Level
fields.sourceQuote: Select a value from Level (Header, Vendor, Line Item, Line Item - Receipt), so the matching rule operates for the field(s) you want compared.
fields.notes: REPAIRED (merge of the three cross-lens twins level_field / level / ruleLevel - one control, one record; level and ruleLevel are listed in dropped). The quote and validValues agree exactly and reproduce THIS file's ASCII-hyphen spelling byte-for-byte. CONTRADICTION - FOUR DIFFERENT ENUMERATIONS ACROSS FOUR TOPICS, RECORDED NOT RECONCILED: (A) FOUR values in the cited step-3 step - Header, Vendor, Line Item, Line Item - Receipt; (B) THREE values in step-3's OWN intro paragraph, same file, same topic - 'Rules-type matching rule sets are based on levels of Vendor, Header, and Line Item'; (C) THREE values in tools-guides/match-rules-and-match-status-8cc2c56b.md - 'They can be specified at the Header, Vendor, or Line Item level, and can be applied on a one-to-one basis between the current invoice and the PO' (that file contains no occurrence of the word 'receipt' at all); (D) four lowercase values in the TRUNCATED create-purchase-order-matching-rules-adb700f9.md. The four-value list is emitted because it is the superset AND because it is the reading whose quote enumerates it; the omissions are likely provisioning-dependent (the receipt level exists only where three-way matching / Concur Receiving is provisioned), but the corpus never says so and this record does not claim it. GROUNDING LANDMINE - THE FOURTH VALUE IS SPELLED THREE WAYS: 'Line Item - Receipt' (ASCII HYPHEN, step-3), 'Line Item – Receipt' (EN DASH, configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md x2 and tools-guides/exceptions-and-three-way-matching-rules-65d52687.md), and 'Line Item-Receipt' (no spaces, final line of that same tools topic). A retyped dash will fail grep -F. Changing Level repopulates the dependent dropdowns: 'As different levels are chosen in Level, different field sets will populate the selections available in Payment Request and Purchase Order.' IDENTIFIER NOTE: the page-scoped name level_field was kept over the bare 'level' to avoid needless collision with the existing page.accounting-administration field labelled 'Level' (segment_level, the account-code hierarchy level) - a different control on a different page that must never be merged with this one.

fields.name: payment_request_field
fields.label: Payment Request
fields.sourceQuote: In the Payment Request list, select the request field to match to the same field in the PO.
fields.notes: REPAIRED. The procedure-lens variant's notes asserted a falsehood - 'no enumerated option list found for any Level value' - which would have told a driver nothing is documented when two conditional enumerations are. That sentence is STRUCK; the tables-lens wording is adopted and both value sets are named explicitly below. On the Rules tab. validValues is deliberately EMPTY: the corpus states the list is repopulated by the Level selection ('As different levels are chosen in Level, different field sets will populate the selections available in Payment Request and Purchase Order') and NEVER enumerates the full catalog for any level. Only two conditional enumerations exist and both are recorded as valueSetCandidates: the Line Item – Receipt pair options, and the source-declared PARTIAL amount-based field list from amounts-and-tolerances ('Line Item Total, Quantity, Tax, Shipping, etc.' - the source itself writes 'etc.'). Field names seen in worked examples elsewhere (Unit Price, Remit Address, Shipping, Quantity, Custom field) are illustrative, not a documented list, and are NOT promoted to values. THE TWO DOCUMENTED CONDITIONAL ENUMERATIONS, spelled out so they cannot be lost again: (1) at the Line Item – Receipt level (EN DASH in the governing Level value there), configure-three-way-matching-c043e5c8.md says 'In the Level list, select Line Item – Receipt, and then, in the Payment Request and Purchase Order lists, select one of the following options:' and enumerates 'Line Quantity and Received Quantity (compares the quantity of the invoice line with the available quantity on the associated receipts)' and 'Receipt Associated and Receipt Associated (checks if the line item is associated with a purchase order line but does not have a receipt associated with it)'. These are PAIRS spanning both dropdowns, and the value set is contextField = Level. (2) the SOURCE-DECLARED PARTIAL amount-based list in amounts-and-tolerances-ab795b1f.md - 'Line Item Total, Quantity, Tax, Shipping, etc.' - where the 'etc.' is the source's own, so that set must stay flagged non-exhaustive and must never be promoted to validValues. validValues stays EMPTY: the full catalog is genuinely never published and is level- and provisioning-dependent by the corpus's own account.

fields.name: group_conditions_dialog
fields.label: Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions
fields.sourceQuote: In Purchase Order Matching Rules Group Conditions, configure the conditions that the system will detect and then execute the matching rule set on
fields.notes: REPAIRED (merge of the cross-lens twins group_conditions_dialog / ruleGroupConditions - one object, one record; ruleGroupConditions is listed in dropped). The name is kept in its '_dialog' form deliberately, because it encodes the containment the refuters required to survive the merge: this is a NESTED WINDOW of this page, not a surface on the rule-set list, and it has no independent click path from Administration. fieldType stays 'unknown' - the corpus never says whether it renders as a grid, a form or a window, though what an admin does there is populate condition rows. ONLY ATTESTATION of this dialog name in the corpus. It is where custom field conditions (e.g. vendor = 'Brooks') that make a Named Rules Group into a condition-based sub-rule are configured. No enumerated field/operator/value list is given - thin is correct here. Reached by: select rule set > Edit > select named rule group > Add. MERGED FROM THE TWIN: conditions are added with Insert and committed with Save; then select the new condition > Edit Rules > (build the rule) > Update > Save. Adding condition groups under a named group is what makes the set a 'Multiple Matching Rule Set'. Condition-based rules run as subsets of the parent rule, and if no condition is met the default rules run (refine-the-rules-include-condition-based-rules-in-a-rule-set-ad7b0d65.md). Tools-guides corroborates the concept: 'Match Rules are configurable, similar to Audit and Workflow rules and can include condition-based rule groups within the overall matching rule set.' HARD WARNING CARRIED FORWARD: the condition operand/field/value catalog is NOT documented for this dialog. Do NOT borrow the 288-bullet catalog from the-condition-page-5d4ea870.md - that is the AUDIT RULES Condition page, a different page already in the graph. Thin is the correct answer here.

fields.name: tolerance
fields.label: Tolerance
fields.sourceQuote: (Optional depending on field choice) Determine what tolerance you will allow when the rule is triggered using options under Tolerance.
fields.notes: REPAIRED. The crosscut variant populated validValues with ONE side of a contradiction the build forbids reconciling (['None','Within (+/-)','Custom','Currency'] - step-3's reading only). validValues is now EMPTY and BOTH readings are recorded with their own verbatim quotes. The Tolerance section of the Rules tab. validValues is deliberately EMPTY because the corpus gives TWO IRRECONCILABLE LISTS for this one control - four options here (None / Within (+/-) / Custom / Currency) and three in configure-three-way-matching (None / Within / Custom). Both are emitted in full as separate valueSetCandidates and the disagreement is recorded as a contradiction; picking one would be reconciling. Note the spelling difference on the second option ('Within (+/-)' vs 'Within') as well as the presence or absence of Currency.
